The test image shows a corn ear/husk with:
- Bleached/tan-to-brown husk coloration
- Premature husk death
- Some dark spots/areas on the husk surface
- Overall brownish-gray discoloration

This looks like an ear rot. Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Diplodia** (bleached husk, pycnidia) or **Ear_rots_Gibberella** (pink/red mold). Let me check the reference.

The reference confirms the match. The test image shows:
- Bleached/tan-to-brown husk with premature death — hallmark of Diplodia ear rot
- Dark spots visible on the husk surface consistent with pycnidia
- The overall husk appearance closely matches the top-left panel of the Diplodia reference (bleached, dying husk)

No pink/red coloring (rules out Gibberella), no green mold (rules out Trichoderma/Aspergillus).
